CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
63-year-old female presents for annual examination. Patient reports depression is well-controlled on current medication with weekly therapy, sleeping 8 hours nightly, and denies suicidal ideation. Regarding hypertension, patient has been checking blood pressure at home with readings that have been fluctuating between high and low over the past couple of weeks without stable readings. Patient reports taking blood pressure medication as prescribed. Patient notes diet has been inconsistent due to work stress and increased hours, resulting in frequent consumption of frozen meals and limited time for grocery shopping and meal preparation. Patient reports some headaches which she attributes to computer screen use at work. Right wrist carpal tunnel release performed approximately 2 years ago has been doing well with no residual numbness or tingling in hands or fingers.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No numbness or tingling in hands or fingers. Headaches present, attributed to computer work. Otherwise reviewed and discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Depression
Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post right wrist carpal tunnel release approximately 2 years ago

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication (lisinopril - to be adjusted)
Depression medication

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works with increased hours and reports high work stress. Diet consists primarily of frozen meals due to time constraints.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs clear. No adenopathy in neck. No hyperthyroidism. Heart regular without murmurs. Grips equal bilaterally. Neurologically intact. Strength good. Pulses good. Overall exam essentially normal. Blood pressure in office today slightly elevated.

RESULTS
Blood pressure slightly elevated in office. Labs essentially normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Hypertension: Blood pressure remains elevated despite current medication compliance. Lisinopril dose increased to 10 mg once daily. Patient instructed to continue monitoring blood pressure at home and return for follow-up in one month to reassess.
2. Depression: Well-controlled on current regimen. No changes to medication at this time. Continue current therapy.
3. Carpal tunnel syndrome: Status post right wrist release doing well. Patient instructed to report any recurrence of tingling or other symptoms.
